why: Some or all of this console's signals are not arriving.
stream.audienceNote: This console checks for this name in every SET's aud and refuses one addressed to anybody else with invalid_audience — recording it either way, so a misaddressed event is visible rather than merely absent.
stream.deliveredToNote: RFC 8935 push, over the loopback interface, with this service's own TLS certificate pinned. It is a real HTTP request on purpose: handing the event to the page in process would skip the body, the media type, the authorization header and the signature.
stream.eventTypesNote: The difference is the intersection SSF 1.0 section 7.1.1 defines: a type this transmitter does not support is answered by its absence from events_delivered rather than by a refusal.
stream.noPush: nothing has been pushed here yet
noStream.before: There is no stream for this console in the “{realm}” realm. It is seeded at startup and is an ORDINARY stream — if it was paused, narrowed or deleted at
noStream.after: or through /admin-api/ssf, it stays that way until a restart. That is the same rule this service's seeded application entries follow.
find.label: Find
find.placeholder: alice, session-revoked, a jti, a stream id
find.what: Over the event name, the type URI, the subject as this receiver read it, the issuer, the audience, the jti and the stream — because a reader arrives holding one of those and does not know which column it is in.
row.more: and {n} more in the same SET
row.noSubject: SSF's own two events are about the STREAM rather than about anybody, so they carry no subject at all. Every CAEP and RISC event does.
row.wrongAudienceTip: This receiver is "{audience}" and that name is not in this token's aud. It was refused with invalid_audience and recorded anyway, because what arrived is the question being asked.
row.mediaTypeTip: RFC 8935 section 2.1 says application/secevent+jwt. This one said "{said}". It was accepted — a receiver that refused would be testing the transmitter's pedantry — and it is said out loud rather than passed over.
reaction.observed: would end this console's sessions (development observes)
row.noMembersTip: Eleven of RISC's fourteen event types have no payload members at all — the SUBJECT carries the entire message, which is why a subject naming the wrong person is a wholly wrong event rather than a partly wrong one.
empty.search: Nothing delivered here matches that search.
empty.none: Nothing has been delivered to this console yet.
heading: Signals received
intro: Every Security Event Token delivered to this console in the “{realm}” realm. This console is a registered Shared Signals receiver: it has a stream of its own, it is POSTed each event over RFC 8935 push at {path}, and it verifies the signature and the audience before recording anything.
copy.head: This is not the transmitter's copy.
copy.ssf: shows every stream this service holds and what it has SENT on each;
copy.rest: show what it BELIEVES about a session and an account. This page shows what came back through the door — which is the only one of the four that goes empty when delivery is broken, and is therefore the only one that can tell you it is.

clear.heading: Clear
clear.before: This drops what is HELD HERE and nothing else. The stream is untouched and goes on delivering, and the
clear.after: 's record of each delivery cannot be cleared — which is the point of it being the durable half.
clear.tip: Drops the {n} delivered event(s) held in this console's inbox in this realm.
